data.text: Cardiology plan update: continue apixaban 5 mg BID without interruption, increase metoprolol tartrate to 37.5 mg BID starting tonight, stop ibuprofen/NSAIDs, use acetaminophen if needed, start magnesium oxide 400 mg nightly for five nights, continue lisinopril 10 mg daily but hold morning dose on procedure day.

prior_context.speaker: nurse_jamison
prior_context.text: Your sister asked at the desk whether the timing changed. I told her only that you are still being evaluated and we have not set the final arrival time.

prior_context.speaker: patient_marcus_reed
prior_context.text: That is exactly what I want. She can know the times later, not the reason anything changes.

prior_context.speaker: clinician_dr_patel
prior_context.text: Hi Marcus, I reviewed the emergency-department tracing and today's ECG. You are still in atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, but you are stable enough for an outpatient rhythm-control plan.

prior_context.speaker: patient_marcus_reed
prior_context.text: Is cardioversion still the plan, or are we trying to just slow the rate?

prior_context.speaker: clinician_dr_patel
prior_context.text: Cardioversion is still the plan. Based on what we know so far, we were aiming for Wednesday morning, but I want the lab results and the medication history fully reconciled first.

prior_context.speaker: clinician_dr_patel
prior_context.text: Until then, continue apixaban 5 milligrams twice daily without interruption. Increase metoprolol tartrate from 25 milligrams twice daily to 37.5 milligrams twice daily starting tonight.

prior_context.speaker: clinician_dr_patel
prior_context.text: Stop ibuprofen and other NSAIDs. Use acetaminophen instead if needed, and start magnesium oxide 400 milligrams nightly for five nights because your previous magnesium trend has been low-normal.

prior_context.speaker: clinician_dr_patel
prior_context.text: Keep lisinopril 10 milligrams daily for now, but hold the morning dose on the day of the procedure once the date is finalized.

prior_context.speaker: patient_marcus_reed
prior_context.text: So right now I keep taking apixaban, I raise the metoprolol tonight, I stop ibuprofen, and I begin the magnesium tonight?

prior_context.speaker: clinician_dr_patel
prior_context.text: Correct. Also do not miss any apixaban doses at all between now and cardioversion.

states.content: Cardioversion remains the plan for Marcus Reed's atrial fibrillation rhythm control, aiming for Wednesday morning, pending lab results and full medication history reconciliation before the cardiologist finalizes the plan. Dr. Patel instructs that Marcus must not miss any apixaban doses at all between now and cardioversion. Nurse Jamison will bring Marcus back first for his cardiology rhythm clinic visit, and Nina can be updated on arrival windows if Marcus keeps the logistics-only setting active. As of the latest update, Marcus is still being evaluated and no final arrival time has been set; Nina asked at the desk whether the timing changed, and Jamison told her only that Marcus is still being evaluated with no final arrival time set.
states.subject: patient_marcus_reed

states.content: Nurse Jamison is reviewing Marcus Reed's medications exactly as he is taking them right now, to prepare an accurate current medication list for review. As part of this review, Nurse Jamison asked Marcus whether he has taken anything over the counter for pain or colds; Marcus reported taking ibuprofen a couple of times last week for shoulder pain before he remembered he probably should not with the blood thinner (apixaban). Dr. Patel has now instructed Marcus to stop ibuprofen and other NSAIDs and to use acetaminophen instead if needed, because NSAIDs raise bleeding risk with apixaban. Nurse Jamison also asked Marcus whether he has missed any doses of apixaban in the last month and whether there were any completely missed doses in the last three weeks; Marcus reported he has not missed any morning doses, reports no completely missed doses in the last three weeks as far as he remembers, and although he might have been a few hours late last Monday night when changing locations, he still took that pill before bed. Marcus also recalls that before cardioversion they were strict about not missing apixaban doses. Nurse Jamison will document the Monday-night apixaban dose as possibly delayed but not skipped. Nurse Jamison further asked Marcus about alcohol, supplements, or stimulants that could affect rhythm; Marcus answered that he does not drink energy drinks.

states.content: Over the past week Marcus Reed has had chest fluttering most evenings, shortness of breath climbing stairs, and one episode of lightheadedness on Saturday; he did not pass out. He also reports no chest pain and no bleeding, but has a racing heartbeat and feels washed out. His presentation is characterized as symptomatic atrial fibrillation/flutter with exertional dyspnea and lightheadedness, and no active bleeding. Clinician Dr. Patel confirms he is still in atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response but is stable enough for an outpatient rhythm-control plan. He had shoulder pain last week, for which he took ibuprofen a couple of times before remembering he probably should not with the blood thinner.
